subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Antennas: Converting Waves to Signals
description: A quick win: understand Antennas: Converting Waves to Signals.

hook.text: An antenna converts electrical current into radio waves for transmission, and back for reception.

buildup.text: The simplest antenna is a dipole — a wire half a wavelength long. It radiates in a donut pattern.

discovery.text: Directional antennas focus energy in one direction — more range toward the target, less waste sideways.

twist.text: Antenna gain doesn't add power — it redirects existing power into a narrower beam.

climax.text: Dish antennas, Yagi arrays, and patch antennas serve satellites, TV, and smartphones respectively.

punchline.text: Antennas don't create power — they aim it where it matters.

quiz.question: What does antenna gain actually do?
options: It amplifies the transmitted power using electronics
It concentrates existing power into a narrower beam for more range in that direction
It increases the frequency of the transmitted signal
